title: Sustained Aerobic Endurance - Vasaloppet Preparation

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Move slowly and deliberately, linking breath to movement. Inhale on cow, exhale on cat. Warm up the spine.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.cues: Control the rotation, feel the hip mobility improving. Switch sides smoothly without rushing.

items.name: Band Pullaparts
items.cues: Use a light resistance band, pull apart with arms extended. Activate shoulders and upper back.

items.name: Rowing Machine - Easy Pace
items.cues: Row at conversational pace, focus on smooth strokes and rhythm. Get heart rate elevated gradually.

items.name: Ski Erg - Steady State
items.cues: Maintain RPE 5-6 (moderate effort, can hold conversation but slightly elevated breathing). Focus on consistent pace and full-body engagement. Think of this as simulating the sustained effort needed for Vasaloppet.

items.name: Rowing Machine - Steady State
items.cues: Continue at RPE 5-6, alternating muscle groups from skiing. Maintain relaxed shoulders and stable core. Keep stroke rate steady at 18-22 strokes per minute.

items.name: Air Bike - Cool Down Pace
items.cues: Easy, low-impact cycling to transition to cooldown. RPE 3-4, allow heart rate to gradually decrease.

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Slow, controlled movements to decompress spine. Focus on breath and letting heart rate normalize.

items.name: Calf Stretch
items.cues: Hold each calf stretch for 30 seconds per leg. Feel the tension release in your lower legs.

items.name: Biceps Wall Stretch
items.cues: Hold each side for 30 seconds. Open up the chest and front shoulders after rowing work.

items.name: Bird Dog
items.cues: Slow, deliberate movements. Engage core without strain. Balance and stabilize on each rep.

rationale: Endurance workout targets aerobic base building essential for Vasaloppet 90km race with 53 days to prepare. RPE 5-6 allows for sustainable, quality work without overtraining.

Multi-modal approach using ski erg and rowing machine mimics cross-country skiing demands while providing recovery variation. Only 1 day since last endurance session, so duration and intensity are appropriately paced.
Mobility-focused warmup and recovery cooldown support longevity training for intermediate athlete, reducing injury risk during build-up phase toward the goal event.
